raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, same as my father. Around here, everyone does wheat in winter and corn in summer — two crops a year on the same fields. The soil here on the North China Plain is good for grain. I don't know why I would change what works.

I have about 8 mu of land. I'll plant all of it to wheat come October, then follow with maize right after the wheat harvest in June. That's the sensible rotation — the ground doesn't sit idle, and I sell both.

For wheat, I'll use the improved seed I buy from the supply cooperative — the same variety as last year, 济麦22 type. I won't bother trying new fancy seeds I don't know. I'll put down plenty of fertilizer at sowing and again at jointing. Water is tight here, so I'll irrigate three times — once before sowing to get moisture in the ground, once at jointing, once around heading. That's what I've always done, and my yields are around 450 jin per mu.

For maize, I'll use hybrid seed — that's just standard now, everyone does. I'll direct-seed straight into the wheat stubble, no plowing needed in summer, that saves time and fuel. Summer usually gets rain, so I'll only irrigate once unless it's very dry.

I apply pesticide twice on wheat — once for weeds in winter, once for aphids and rust in spring. Maize just needs one spray for stem borer.
